cohort: The study included women with low-risk, singleton, term-gestation (>=37 weeks), cephalic presentation first births, using vital records data from the National Center for Health Statistics.
finding: The study found a strong association between an excessive rate of gestational weight gain and an increased risk of cesarean delivery, irrespective of prepregnancy body mass index.
mod_finding: Excessive gestational weight gain was associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery, regardless of prepregnancy BMI, with appropriate weight gain potentially offering a protective effect for those with a healthy prepregnancy BMI.
cross-section timing: At the time of birth, as captured in vital records
